I mean… the Unity/Bunker is only SLIGHTLY less crazy awesome than the actual French people that came over to fight. I mean, Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier had a long family history of trouble making and badass-ness.

Also, plate armor totally works. It was developed in response to bullets, so having one that has some special metallurgy that keeps it bullet-proof even after the 1500s isn’t much of a stretch for super-hero physics.

I like how they did the 1776, overall. I can see an alternate universe based on that in the same groove as Marvel 1602.

posts.name: FrivYeti
posts.cooked:
I’m a bit surprised that C&A didn’t notice that they’d successfully referenced seven members of the Freedom Five (plus Unity) in their Freedom Four!

First, obviously, Legacy. They discussed the Tachyon elements in Meredith Montgomery, making her both Tachyon and the Wraith. And L’Unité was both Bunker and Unity in a new, fancy cannon.

But Icebear is also two different people. He’s got the cold powers and standoffish attitude of Absolute Zero, but he’s also a member of an Indigenous nation who was abandoned by his people after they thought he died, and now he’s a loner who travels with others temporarily but has no people to call his own while being a big bear of a guy. He’s Absolute Zero and Haka, bringing in another founding Freedom Five member!

If only there’d been a way to fit the Shrieker in there…

posts.cooked: Well the Tachyon element of Meredith Montgomery was basically just her name; I think it was the right call not to try and do a speedster in the past, since that’s inherently a very modern-feeling power (speed of transit is one of the things, akin to computing power, that has just steadily gone up and up and up since the relevant technologies first appeared). posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
It was initially said by Adam to someone at a PAX Unplugged event then confirmed on air in later podcast episodes.

In Publisher’s Note #3 for instance:

  • A recent conversation about the location of Megalopolis brought to mind the fact that the location of Rook City has been discussed, but not in the podcast; the rumor mill placed it in Pennsylvania - given its industrial background and other similarities, is it a fictional stand-in for Pittsburgh? Christopher’s response is to just show us the Google Maps overlay they’d put together for it. We have permission to share screenshots, so here is my quick and dirty collection of images. Rather than being a Pittsburgh stand-in, it’s right on the border with New Jersey (with some locations technically being in NJ) on the Delaware River near the real-life locations of Levittown, PA and Trenton, NJ. Similar maps exist for both Megalopolis and Mordengrad, but we don’t see them today. [A later question asks what software was used to generate the map - it’s just done within Google Maps.]
